Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroTech Dynamics Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroTech Dynamics' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Strategy Officer; and Emily Vargas, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

David Reynolds:
Thank you, John, and good morning. AeroTech Dynamics delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense systems, space, and aftermarket services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, I'll cover several key areas central to our results: our book-to-bill ratio overall and by segment; potential risks and opportunities; updates on key programs like NGAD, hypersonics, and space systems; program margins and cost performance; the defense budget outlook and its impact; performance of our priority defense programs; and major new contract awards.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to position us as the leader in next-generation air dominance for future growth. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily. Let me start with updates on our key programs, where execution has been disciplined despite ongoing challenges.

Our funded backlog stands at $125 billion, up 8% year-over-year, providing strong revenue visibility with over 60% deliverable in the next 24 months. We're addressing supply chain issues like titanium shortages from Russian sanctions and labor constraints at facilities in Fort Worth and Palmdale through dual-sourcing with U.S. and allied suppliers such as Allegheny Technologies, keeping delays under 2%.

In our Next Generation Air Dominance family, including the F-47 stealth fighter and Collaborative Combat Aircraft drones, we're on track for Risk Reduction Phase 3 by Q4 2025. We've invested $1.2 billion in FY24 R&D for adaptive cycle engines from GE and Pratt & Whitney, improving fuel efficiency by 25%. Digital twins with Siemens NX have cut design iterations by 40%, and additive manufacturing supports rapid prototyping. We got LRIP Lot 4 approval worth $4.8 billion, totaling $18.7 billion in bookings. Production is at 4 F-47s per month in Greenville, aiming for 14 by 2027 for 185 units. First flight slipped slightly due to avionics with AN/APG-85 radar, resolved via BAE's GaN modules, tested on XQ-58A Valkyrie with 250 hours this quarter. Exports are strong: Australia committed $2.1 billion for 32 F-47s and 50 CCAs under AUKUS, deliveries from 2026. UAE FMS talks advance. Margins at 12.5% in LRIP, expanding to 14-15% at FRP.

In hypersonics, Dark Eagle boost-glide and Black Widow scramjet exceed Mach 20 over 1,800 nautical miles. Flight test #7 from Kauai validated carbon-carbon TPS from Materion at 3,000°F with minimal ablation, using DARPA Glide Breaker and Palantir AI guidance. Army awarded $3.2 billion LRIP Lot 2 plus 120 more units, production at 8 per month in Tucson up 50% YoY, IOC Q1 2025, backlog $7.9 billion. UK MoD selected for Global Combat Air Programme at $1.1 billion. Margins up to 11.2% via learning curves and Raytheon cost-sharing.

For Space Systems, Vanguard LEO constellation for SDA hit Tranche 2 Launch 1 with 28 satellites via SpaceX, 100% checkout in 72 hours, OISLs at 100 Gbps using L3Harris photonics, cutting mass 30% and power 25%. Production at 12 per month in Redondo Beach and Azusa, $2.9 billion new from USSF PWSA, backlog $11.4 billion plus NRO. NATO ESA $500 million for data fusion. Margins 16.8% from COTS and reusable launches.

On MQ-Next UCAV for Replicator, 85% digital engineering with Anduril AI for Level 4 autonomy, Q4 award for 200 units at $28 million each.

These position us for 25% share in $100 billion NGAD/hypersonics/LEO market by 2030 per Teal Group, with $15 billion international pipeline. Investments in supply chains and upskilling target 95% on-time delivery. Program revenue growth 12-15%, margins 11-13%.

We've also secured major new contract awards that underscore this momentum. In Q3, $4.7 billion in bookings pushed backlog to $28.5 billion, up 22% YoY, funded $3.2 billion, book-to-bill 1.8x from our $15 billion pipeline.

NGAD Phase 2 $2.1 billion from USAF for digital engineering, building on $850 million Phase 1, for PCA and CCA swarms with ATLAS AI for 95% survivability. IDIQ ceiling $20 billion, teaming RTX and Northrop. Reduces F-35 reliance, taps $21 billion budget. AUKUS Australia $500 million potential.

Hypersonics: $1.2 billion sole-source GPI LRIP from MDA, post Mach 7 test, 40% smaller/cheaper than SM-3, for Zumwalt/Virginia, up 150% YoY bookings. Japan co-production FY25.

Space: SDA $750 million PWSA Tranche 2 for 36 O2C terminals with Hall thrusters, 10 Gbps low latency. USSF $450 million DEW prototyping with 300kW lasers. Space 20% backlog.

FMS: Saudi $200 million Patriot GEM-T GaN radars. Army $450 million HIMARS munitions.

These reflect multi-domain focus, $50 billion IDIQs, 40% JV bookings, 25%+ margins post-LRIP via MBSE. FY24 bookings $10-12 billion, raised revenue $7.8-8.2 billion, EPS $6.75-7.25.

Sarah, over to you for the financial details.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, David. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $7.5 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.10. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $8.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at $28-29 billion revenue, 10-11% operating margins, and $4.2-4.4 billion free cash flow. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Specific financial highlights include gross margin of 23%, operating income of $1.25 billion, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion.

As we dive deeper, one key leading indicator is our book-to-bill ratio, both overall and by segment—a strong barometer of demand and future growth amid supply chain normalization, geopolitical tailwinds, and next-gen ramps. Overall for Q3, we achieved 1.18x, our ninth straight quarter above 1.0x, up from 1.12x last Q3 and 1.15x Q2. Year-to-date 1.20x, with $12.4 billion new orders vs. $10.3 billion revenue, driving funded backlog to record $148 billion, up 14% YoY, averaging over four years visibility.

By segment: Commercial Aerospace at 1.05x Q3 ($4.2B booked vs. $4.0B revenue), YTD 1.08x, rebounding with air travel at 105% of 2019 RPKs per IATA. Wins: 45 firm AeroJet 900X orders from Asia-Pacific LCCs amid A320neo constraints. Regional: NA 55%, Europe 25%, APAC 15%, India/SE Asia offsetting widebody softness. $1.2B in sustainable tech with GE, for ICAO 2030 mandates.

Defense Systems stellar at 1.32x Q3 ($5.1B vs. $3.9B), YTD 1.35x, best in peers like Lockheed/Northrop. Geopolitics accelerating: $2.8B Sentinel II hypersonic IDIQ, $1.5B F-35 Lot 16. DoD 70%, FMS NATO 20% Poland/Australia. Europe +25% YoY Ukraine aid. Digital engineering cuts cycles 30% via MBSE.

Space & Missiles 1.22x Q3 ($2.3B vs. $1.9B), YTD 1.25x. $1.1B NSSL Phase 3 Lane 2 vs. SpaceX/Blue Origin. $900M Orion successor Artemis milestones. USG 85%, ESA/JAXA 10%. SRM headwinds mitigated by composites vertical integration, 15% overrun avoidance. Cislunar $100B by 2030 per McKinsey.

Aftermarket & Services 1.10x ($800M vs. $730M), YTD 1.12x. Fleet utilization 85% per Cirium. MRO C-130J/F-16 60%, digital twins 98% retention. Middle East +30% F-15EX Saudi.

Forward, 1.15-1.25x through 2025, $20B FY24 awards incl. NGAD, commercial China. Risks: machining labor, titanium disruptions; $500M reshoring with Spirit. Bolsters FCF $6-7B 2025.

Shifting to program margins and cost performance across Aeronautics, Missiles & Fire Control, and Space. Segment-adjusted operating margins expanded 120 bps to 11.8% Q3, from mix, cost-outs, EVM gains on $125B backlog, $48B funded.

Aeronautics (42% revenue) 12.4% up from 11.1%, above 12% target. F-35 Lots 15/16 CPI 1.05, closed $120M variance, $450M affordability via Lightning Smart: digital twins cut wing labor 18%, AM titanium 25% savings. Margins 13.2%, Lots 17-18 $78M/F-35A, -6% unit. KC-46A 9.8% CPI 1.02, $85M RVS offset by $200M contract, SPI 0.98. US DoD $12.5B FY25 F-35s, FMS Israel/Poland $1.2B, Europe NATO +$3B potential.

MFC 14.1% +250 bps, hypersonics/replen. LRASM/JASSM-ER 15.5% CPI 1.12, $150M GaN savings 30% RF. 550 missiles/year $2.8B multi-year. Hypersonics 8.2% $65M EAC TPS, Agile MBSE +40% testing SPI 1.03, Raytheon/Northrop shares. Rare earths +2% YoY, dual-source 85%. AUKUS HIMARS Australia $800M 13% margins.

Space 10.3% +180 bps, backlog $28B +15%. GPS IIIF/STPSat CPI 1.08 11.5%, zero-based $90M NRE cut, laser comms -22%. GEO 9.7% $40M radiation fix, Orion AI factory +25% throughput. USSF $30B FY25, China ASAT spurring LEO, $4-5B wins.

Portfolio CPI 1.06 + from 0.99, +$320M variances, 85% learning F-35, inflation 3.2% passed 65% cost-plus. $1.2B saved enterprise via portals/RPA. 92% green EVM fixed-price, CRADAs DARPA. 5,000 hires, titanium +40%.

Company-wide 11.5-11.8% FY24, 12.5% 2025 volume.

On the defense budget outlook, global spending hits $2.4T 2024 per SIPRI +6.8%, Ukraine/Taiwan/Red Sea/Iran drivers. US FY25 request $849.8B base +4.1% +$116B OCO = $965B. NDAA bipartisan, air/hypersonics +12% $38B our ARROW $2.1B LRIP Q4. BMD +8% $11.2B PAC-3/GPI. O&M 42% $361B F-35 ALIS/ODIN $14.5B.

FRA caps 1%, shift OCO/UPLs $450M drones. Europe NATO 2% 18/32, $380B +17%, Poland F-35 $10B, Germany CH-53K $3.2B, backlog $12.7B +22% FMS 115%. Indo-Pac China $225B, AUKUS $4B, Japan GCAP digital twins $3.2B, Taiwan $19B HIMARS/TPY-4. ME Israel Iron Dome $1.8B, GCC $50B IAMD.

Backlog $78.4B +14% 1.28x book-to-bill, unfunded $42B JADC2. Aeronautics $4.2B +11% 142 jets 98% quality, NGAD $1.1B. Missiles/Space $2.8B +25% ARROW Mach 12, SDA $850M. Integrated $650M DEW TRL-8. Margins 12.4%, IRAD $420M digital/PT6.5. Raised FY24 $28.5-29.2B +7%, EBITDA $4.1-4.3B. FY25 9-11%. Pillars: Replicator 1,000 drones, MBSE 30% cycles, F-35 co-prod Japan/Poland 15% FMS.

Turning to performance of priority defense programs, driving 62% sales $2.8B +18% YoY, margins 14.2% +220 bps FRP ramps, digital, mix. F-35 sustain/Block 4 28 Lot 17 jets, FY 110-120, $1.1B +12% $4.2B Lots 18-20. Margins 11.5% titanium dual Leonardo, FMS Israel/Poland $450M 32 jets NATO.

NGAD FoS 75% digital MBSE -30% cycle, $850M AFRL adaptive/CCA, $25B IDIQ FY26 ahead Boeing engines.

Hypersonics HGV Navy-cross LRHW-like, Kauai test #3 June, $2.1B FRP 150 $650M +25% 16.8% -18% unit reusable. NGI 98% hit GMD, UAE $900M Patriot, Japan hypersonic MoU.

Unmanned MQ-Next RQ-4 $1.5B spiral $320M 50/month Palantir AIP 4:1 kills White Sands, $7B MUX 20% cost edge Anduril.

pLEO SDA Tranche 2 18 sats FOC $280M $3.8B backlog 10 Gbps >Starshield, ESA Artemis €200M.

R&D $1.2B +15% SOSA/UCI -25% integration, Alabama composites -22% F-35 wings. Labor/RF GaN challenges, 12/12/12 95%. Backlog $52B +22% 40% funded, Q3 16-20% $11-11.5B 13-15%.

Before Q&A, on risks and opportunities per 10-Q/K, safe harbor. Diversified fixed-wing, rotary, C4ISR, hypersonics, space for mid-high single-digit CAGR FY27.

Opportunities: FY24 NDAA $886B +4.2%, F-35 Lots 16-18 $2.1B Block 4 EW APG-85, 28% NGAD share $1.8B CCA IDIQ. B-21 $203B LRIP 3/year FY26 backlog $12.4B +18%.

Hypersonics HAWC hit March, HACM $1.5B, 300kW laser 45% eff. REplicator $800M.

Space GPS IIIF M-code, $4.2B 72 VLEO ISR, Blue Origin New Glenn $500M.

Europe 2% Poland F-35 $12B Germany CH-53K $3.2B. Indo-Pac AUKUS $2-3B hypersonic/quantum, ME F-15EX Saudi $5B.

Commercial 737/A320 MRO +22% $1.1B LEAP San Antonio 95% SAF 15% margins.

R&D $1.2B 12% sales autonomy JADC2 digital twins -20% LRIP, M&A GaN $300-500M 35% EBITDA.

Risks ERM FAR/DFARS: Supply titanium +35% F-35 skins 3-4 mo $150M, semis 52w E-7. Dual 70% Tier1 $400M stockpile DPA, 50bps EBITDA.

Geopol Ukraine USAI $900M 15% delays, Taiwan SM-6 ITAR 15 licenses, Houthi +8% shipping.

Inflation CPI 3.1% composites B-21 +12%, welders +22% $50M apprenticeship 1,200 hires, 200-300bps if >5% wages.

Cyber Volt Typhoon CMMC zero-trust NIST zero, FCF KC-46 $220M overrun.

Compet RTX PrSM Boeing T-7A, but 45% win $50B recompetes.

Opps > risks, FY24 guidance intact, $7B liquidity 1.8x leverage $1B repurchase.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, dual-sourcing critical materials and reshoring with partners to counter disruptions, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 and NGAD by 20%. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies, including AI predictive maintenance and robotic assembly lines, to improve efficiency, reduce costs by 15%, and achieve 95% on-time delivery.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. On the technology front, we're making significant strides in next-generation propulsion systems like adaptive cycle engines and hypersonic scramjets, achieving 25% better efficiency and Mach 20+ capabilities. Our solid-state lasers at 300kW and photonic circuits for space are ahead of thresholds, giving us a competitive edge through AI autonomy and MBSE tools that cut development cycles by 30-40%.

Robert Hayes:
Thank you, Lisa. From a strategic perspective, we are actively evaluating potential acquisitions in gallium nitride RF and composites for $300-500 million to complement our portfolio and expand market reach into cislunar and Indo-Pacific allies. We are also developing new business models around proliferated LEO and attritable drones to capture Replicator and AUKUS opportunities, targeting 25% share in $100 billion markets.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Josh Green with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Green:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the book-to-bill ratio in the defense systems segment and how it compares to peers?

David Reynolds:
Certainly, Josh. As Sarah detailed, defense systems hit 1.32x in Q3, YTD 1.35x, leading peers like Lockheed and Northrop, driven by Sentinel II, F-35 Lot 16, and geopolitical urgency from Ukraine, Middle East, and Indo-Pacific. DoD 70%, FMS NATO strong, with digital engineering enabling quick wins in FY25 $850 billion topline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about supply chain risks, particularly titanium and semis, and mitigation progress?

Sarah Kline:
Maria, great question. Titanium spiked 35% from Russia sanctions delaying F-35 skins, semis 52 weeks for E-7 ASICs. We've dual-sourced 70-85% Tier 1s, stockpiled $400 million criticals, invoked DPA, and invested $500 million reshoring with Spirit and Allegheny—limiting EBITDA hit to 50 bps, inventories up 40%, keeping CPI above 1.05 portfolio-wide.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly:
Regarding the NGAD program milestones and any slippage risks?

Lisa Patel:
Tom, NGAD is on track for Phase 3 Q4 2025, LRIP Lot 4 $4.8 billion ramping to 14/month by 2027. Minor avionics slip resolved with GaN, Valkyrie surrogate 250 hours validating. Digital twins and MBSE derisked, AUKUS exports adding momentum—margins expanding to 14-15% FRP.

David Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

John Smith:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
